title: Amazon ECS Gateway Arrives with Generated Hostnames and No Custom Domain Support
partialText: <img src="https://www.infoq.com/styles/static/images/logo/logo_bigger.jpg"/><p>AWS has released Amazon ECS Gateway, an account-level ingress resource letting platform teams define networking once and application teams opt services in with a connector. Each service gets a generated hostname and routing is host-based, and neither the announcement nor the documentation covers custom domains.</p> <i>By Steef-Jan Wiggers</i>

title: Docker Urges Isolation and Governance for AI Agent Security
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/11/docker-ai-agent-security/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1793733720293.jpg"/><p>Docker has published a guide to five security risks that arise when AI agents are allowed to browse, run code and call tools with limited human oversight. They argue that the autonomy that makes agents useful also makes conventional application security controls insufficient. The company positions isolation and governance, rather than model improvements alone, as the main defences.</p> <i>By Matt Saunders</i>

title: LinkedIn Uses OpenTelemetry to Trace the Member Journey from Tap to Backend
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/11/linkedin-opentelemetry-journey/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1793095474316.jpg"/><p>LinkedIn has built an OpenTelemetry-based telemetry platform that connects what members do in its iOS, Android, and web applications with the backend services processing those interactions.</p> <i>By Craig Risi</i>

title: Shopify Overexposed Scans GKE Ingresses and Cloud Run for Exposure
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/11/shopify-kubernetes-ingresses/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1793520999206.jpg"/><p>Shopify has introduced Overexposed. This internal scanner locates Kubernetes Ingresses on GKE and Cloud Run services. It checks for those that are accessible from the internet without authentication.</p> <i>By Claudio Masolo</i>

title: AWS Capacity Largely Sold out through 2027, with On-Demand Headroom Reserved
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/11/aws-capacity-sold-out/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1793124716899.jpg"/><p>Amazon CEO Andy Jassy says AWS’s large committed cloud capacity is largely sold out through 2027, with part of 2028 already allocated, while the company continues to reserve headroom for On Demand, EC2 and Bedrock. Practitioners discussing the remarks report difficulty obtaining On Demand capacity for ordinary EC2 instances, and similar constraints at other providers.</p> <i>By Steef-Jan Wiggers</i>

title: File Mover Express: AWS Releases Open-Source Tool for S3 File Transfers
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/11/aws-s3-file-transfer/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1792218946629.jpg"/><p>AWS has recently released File Mover Express, an open-source application under the Apache 2.0 license for transferring large files between local systems and Amazon S3. Available for macOS, Windows, and Linux, it supports parallel transfers, automatic performance tuning, retries, pause and resume, and file integrity verification.</p> <i>By Renato Losio</i>

title: Cloudflare’s Post-Quantum GeoKey Manager Enters Closed Beta without Attribute-Based Encryption
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/10/cf-pq-geokey-manager/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1793376907936.jpg"/><p>Cloudflare has moved a post-quantum rebuild of GeoKey Manager into closed beta, guarding geo-fenced keys with hybrid ML-KEM-768 and X25519 instead of the attribute-based encryption used since 2022. Keys live only in kernel memory on verified regional servers, and any failed check rejects the request, a fail-closed choice practitioners ask could cause a regional outage. GA is planned for Q1 2027.</p> <i>By Steef-Jan Wiggers</i>

title: Kubernetes Confidential Containers Get Fortanix Attestation and Key Management
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/10/k8s-confidential-containers/en/headerimage/header-1793049721702.jpeg"/><p>Fortanix's CoCo integration connects workload attestation to decryption-key release for Kubernetes AI workloads. GPU-verification settings affect protection, while upstream Trustee and Azure Secure Key Release offer alternative routes to attestation-based key release.</p> <i>By Mark Silvester</i>

title: LocalStack for Azure Enters Public Preview with Security Settings Stored but Not Enforced
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/10/localstack-azure-preview/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1793037893055.jpg"/><p>LocalStack has opened its Azure emulator to a free public preview, running Azure services locally and accepting existing ARM, Bicep, and Terraform without rewrites. Its own documentation reports partial operation coverage per service and a consistent pattern: configuration is stored and returned, while enforcement of access restrictions, TLS, and network rules is not implemented.</p> <i>By Steef-Jan Wiggers</i>

title: Netflix Treats GPU Reliability as a Distributed Systems Problem
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/10/netflix-gpu-distributed-systems/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1792576903003.jpg"/><p>Netflix has detailed how it is building a reliability platform for large-scale GPU training and inference, using layered health checks, automated remediation, and fault-tolerant training to keep jobs running despite hardware failures.</p> <i>By Craig Risi</i>

title: Netflix Titus Adds Single-Tenant VM Isolation for Containers
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/10/netflix-titus-kubernetes-microvm/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1793268697529.jpg"/><p>Netflix has added single-tenant Titus, a mode that runs one task alone on its own right-sized EC2 instance. The Compute/Platform team still owns and patches the host, so application teams keep the same API and deployment path</p> <i>By Claudio Masolo</i>

title: Microsoft Retires Azure Deployment Environments with No Replacement Product
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/10/ade-dev-box-retirement/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1792499241111.jpg"/><p>Azure Deployment Environments retires on February 22, 2027 and Microsoft names no successor, telling teams to use Bicep or ARM templates directly. Microsoft Dev Box follows on September 18, 2028, pointed at Windows 365, which Microsoft says is not a one-to-one replacement. Remaining Dev Box workloads should expect deletion.</p> <i>By Steef-Jan Wiggers</i>

title: Bug0 Releases QA Agent to Automate Regression Testing with Cached Playwright Replays
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/10/bug0-agent-testing-cached-replay/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1793286673185.jpg"/><p>QA Agent is a new source-available Playwright library for agentic browser regression testing. The agent associates test instructions expressed in natural language to actions on the user interface, caches those when appropriate for faster CI replays, remapping them to test specifications when the user interface changes. Verification is based on multi-model consensus and vision model evaluations.</p> <i>By Bruno Couriol</i>

title: Datadog Builds a Specialist AI Model for SRE Investigations
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/10/datadog-scout-sre-model/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1793038066919.jpg"/><p>Datadog has released Scout, a model trained to investigate production problems. It runs inside Bits Investigation, the company's AI SRE product, where it can pick up an alert, look through telemetry and suggest what caused the problem. Datadog engineers and a small number of customers are using it in a closed preview.</p> <i>By Matt Saunders</i>

title: Presentation: Wrangling Telemetry at Scale: a Guide to Self-Hosted Observability
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/presentations/self-hosted-observability-stack-tradeoffs/en/mediumimage/colin-douch-medium-1791450600829.jpeg"/><p>Colin Douch shares battle-tested strategies for building and scaling self-hosted observability stacks. He explains how to effectively correlate metrics, structured logs, and distributed traces using open-source tooling like Prometheus, VictoriaMetrics, and Jaeger, while navigating the engineering trade-offs of avoiding SaaS vendor lock-in.</p> <i>By Colin Douch</i>
